quiz.q: What is the official, recommended way to install Rust?
options: Downloading rustc.exe from a random site
quiz.explain: rustup (from rustup.rs) is the official installer. It installs and updates rustc and cargo and can switch toolchains.

quiz.q: You just installed Rust but your terminal says 'command not found' for cargo. What's the most likely fix?
options: Open a new terminal so the PATH change takes effect
Delete rustup and use apt instead
quiz.explain: An already-open terminal doesn't see the new PATH. Opening a fresh terminal (or sourcing ~/.cargo/env) usually fixes it.

quiz.q: Which command confirms the compiler is installed and reachable?
quiz.explain: rustc --version prints the compiler's version number, confirming it's installed and on your PATH.

quiz.q: How do you update to the latest stable Rust after it's installed?
options: You must reinstall from scratch each time
quiz.explain: rustup update fetches the latest stable rustc and cargo and swaps them in. Rust releases roughly every six weeks.

flashcards.front: What tool installs and updates Rust, and where do you get it?
flashcards.back: rustup, from rustup.rs. It manages rustc and cargo and keeps them updated.

flashcards.front: After installing Rust, why might 'cargo' still be 'command not found'?
flashcards.back: Your open terminal hasn't picked up the new PATH. Open a new terminal (or run: source "$HOME/.cargo/env").

flashcards.front: How do you verify the install worked?
flashcards.back: Run rustc --version and cargo --version — both should print a version number.
